title: In‐dia for the Long Haul
summary:
In‐dia for the Long Haul
The high crude oil price environment seen in 2011 has raised concern that inflationary pressure could interfere with the pace of global economic recovery. Some developing economies have attempted to control runaway inflation by limiting the price of fuel sold to domestic consumers, but just over a year ago, India began phasing out its subsidies for transportation fuels. The Finance Ministry acknowledged that the removal of subsidies would likely bring about an increase in inflation in the near term.

children.title: The Rest is West
children.summary: In addition to taking steps to make fuel prices more market driven, India has also implemented product specifications similar to the Euro III and Euro IV standard, ostensibly as a way to improve air quality and adhere to stricter environmental standards domestically. The tightening of quality has facilitated marketing of Indian transportation fuels to consuming nations in Europe and the United States on long range product tankers, which offer greater economies of scale for these long‐haul voyages compared to smaller MR sized product tankers.
